reason: Same root cause as status-4 and annot-6. sync.sh:100/:361 reads through an fd opened on the original inode, and :367 runs `mv "$tmp" "$file"` unconditionally, even on a no-op pass. There is no lock anywhere in lib/ or bin/ (rg flock/.lock finds nothing). Every other mutator replaces the inode by tmp+mv (resolve.sh:153, defer.sh:172, annotate.sh:173/:542, promote.sh:73, archive.sh:150), so any of those writes that lands mid-sync is reverted. The post-bash-dispatch.sh:14-23 ordering claim only covers the sync that hook spawns itself. One caveat: `log` appends with `>>` to the same inode (log.sh:212), so a log written while sync is still mid-loop gets read and kept. Only a log landing after EOF and before the mv is lost.
fix: Minimal: skip the write when nothing changed (`cmp -s "$tmp" "$file" || mv ...`), and use optimistic concurrency: capture `cksum <"$file"` before the loop and re-check it right before mv. If it changed, discard tmp. Unattended runs exit quietly; an explicit sync re-runs once. A mkdir-lock that every mutator shares is the full fix, but sync must not hold it across gh network calls.
repro: Use a stub gh that sleeps 5s on a ledger with one (PR: o/r#1) entry. Run `found-issues sync &`, then after 1s run `found-issues resolve <other entry>` or `defer` (not `log`, which appends to the same inode and usually survives). After `wait`, the resolve/defer is gone.

reason: sync.sh:93 and the other mutators (archive.sh:139, resolve.sh:139, defer.sh:146, annotate.sh:150/:529, parse-entries.sh:684/:785, promote.sh:57) all create the tmp with `mktemp -t` in $TMPDIR. The mode change is deterministic: mktemp makes the file 0600 and mv keeps the source mode, so the ledger becomes 0600, and a symlinked ledger is replaced by a regular file. Git does not track 0644 vs 0600, so there is no diff noise. Cross-device non-atomicity depends on the platform (tmpfs /tmp on Fedora/Arch, TEMP on C: with the repo on D:). For KB-sized files the truncated-read window is tiny, so real loss needs a crash or ENOSPC mid-copy. Grade low. codex-hooks.sh:171 already uses the correct same-directory pattern.
fix: `tmp="$(mktemp "$(dirname "$file")/.found-issues.XXXXXX")"`, as codex-hooks.sh:171 already does. Optionally restore the mode with the same original_mode approach statusline-install.sh:435 uses. The dot-prefixed tmp is removed by the existing EXIT traps.

reason: archive.sh:148 runs `grep -F -x -v -f ... >"$tmp" || true`, which swallows exit status 2, and :150 mv's the result with no check. Unlike parse-entries.sh:51 it does not set LC_ALL=C or -a. The finder overstates the scope. GNU grep >=3.5 in a UTF-8 locale suppresses only the lines containing invalid encoding (message goes to stderr, exit 0), so the bad-byte [open] entry itself is deleted from the ledger and never archived. A NUL suppresses everything after it, and grep <3.5 writes 'Binary file matches' to stdout, i.e. into the ledger. Silent data loss, but it needs a rare trigger (cp1252 bytes pasted on Git Bash, truncated UTF-8). Since v2.9.1 archive only runs on explicit sync/archive.
fix: `LC_ALL=C grep -a -F -x -v -f ...`. Capture rc and abort before mv when rc>1. Assert that the tmp line count equals the original count minus archived_count. The ledger-15 fix (awk delete by NR) subsumes this.
repro: Ledger with `- [fixed] 2020-01-01 a.sh:1 — old (fixed: 2020-01-02)` plus `printf -- '- [open] 2026-10-01 b.sh:1 — bad \xff byte\n' >>`. Run `LANG=en_US.UTF-8 found-issues archive` with GNU grep and check whether the [open] line survives in docs/found-issues.md.

reason: archive.sh:69 and :71 depend on ERE interval expressions `{4}`/`{2}` inside a plain `awk` call. mawk 1.3.4-20200120 (Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04 default awk) does not support repetitions, so both matches fail, fixed_pairs is empty, and :111-112 print 'nothing to archive' with 'fixed entries: 0'. PR CI is ubuntu-latest (24.04, mawk 20240123 with intervals) and macOS (bwk awk with intervals), so neither would catch it. Elsewhere the code already avoids regex portability traps in awk (parse-entries.sh:325-327).
fix: Replace the intervals with `[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]` in both match() calls. Add a bats case that forces `awk` to mawk when one is available.
repro: On Debian 12 / Ubuntu 22.04 without gawk: `printf -- '- [fixed] 2020-01-01 a — b (fixed: 2020-01-02)\n' | awk '{print match($0,/\(fixed: [0-9]{4}-/)}'` prints 0. Then `found-issues archive --days 1` reports 'fixed entries: 0'.

reason: Fork sources verified: sync.sh:106 runs `$(fi_parse_entry)`, inside which parse-entries.sh:109 is printf|sed, :199 is `$(fi_annotation_tail)`, and :203-247 are six printf|grep|sed|paste pipelines. sync.sh:107-112 add five printf|grep|head|cut re-splits. sync.sh:239 runs `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` per entry although the value is loop-invariant. The :254 guard is always true because e_path is the first whitespace token (parse-entries.sh:136), so the :255 sed runs for every path-like entry, including ones whose file exists. :164/:165/:175 spawn three jq per PR. SessionStart runs this synchronously (session-start.sh:366).
fix: Low-risk subset first: hoist repo_root above the loop; move the recovered_loc block inside `[[ ! -e "$full_path" ]]`; replace :107-112 with one `while IFS= read -r kv; do case ${kv%%=*} in path) ...; esac; done <<<"$e_data"` (the pattern at parse-entries.sh:585-607); collapse the three jq calls into one `gh pr view --json state,baseRefName,mergedAt --jq '[.state,.baseRefName,.mergedAt]|@tsv'` read into three vars. The builtin parser rewrite is worthwhile but larger.

reason: For an entry whose path is missing and contains '/' or '.', sync.sh:286-291 calls fi_detect_rename. That runs a whole-history `git log --diff-filter=R -M --name-status` plus 2 awk (bin/found-issues:182-190) before the cheap tracked-ever check in fi_git_confirms_removed (:161/:165). Abstract locations are never tombstoned (never tracked), so they pay this cost on every sync forever. Correction: the call happens twice only for spaced locations (recovered_loc is empty otherwise, :259), so the cost is K calls, not 2K, for typical abstract tokens.
fix: Before fi_detect_rename, skip both rename and tombstone when `git log -1 --format=%H -- "$path"` is empty. A rename source must have been tracked, so this changes no outcome. Optionally memoize `renames` in a global for the whole sync.

reason: sync.sh:148 (and :133) require `command -v jq`, and gh_empty_warnings is only filled inside that block (:160), so on a gh-without-jq machine merged PRs never close and nothing is printed. Graded low because missing jq is a documented fail-open (docs/architecture.md:258). post-bash-dispatch.sh:56 also exits without jq, so on such a machine PR annotations only arrive from other machines' commits. :139 shows gh's built-in --jq already works.
fix: Drop the jq gate on both blocks: use `gh pr view --json state,baseRefName,mergedAt --jq '[.state,.baseRefName,.mergedAt]|@tsv'` and split the result via read (shared with the ledger-5 fix). The same applies to bin/found-issues:287/:312 (`gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq .defaultBranchRef.name`).

reason: (a) detect-mode.sh:90 runs `gh auth status`, which validates the token against the API, before the 1h cache check at :106-114. sync (:67), log/resolve/defer/promote-deferred (via bin/found-issues:221) and doctor all pay it. (b) sync.sh:156 and :139 issue one `gh pr view` per entry per PR with no per-run dedupe. (c) bin/found-issues:312 has no negative cache: when origin/HEAD is unset and the gh fetch fails, every sync retries the network call. All of this sits on the synchronous SessionStart path (session-start.sh:366), which has no timeout.
fix: Move the cache-file check above `gh auth status` (a stale-auth cached mode just degrades to gh_empty warnings). Memoize pr_ref→tsv in a newline-delimited string per sync. Write an empty negative-cache stamp (e.g. 10 min TTL) when the gh default-branch lookup fails.

reason: The cwd half is largely refuted. Both installed snippets do `cd "$__FI_DIR" && status --cwd "$__FI_DIR"` precisely so the background `$0 sync` (list-status.sh:177) inherits the workspace as PWD (statusline-install.sh:420-422 and the append form, statusline-target.sh:166/:200). A mismatch remains only in the no-jq fallback branch and in hand-rolled statuslines that pass --cwd without cd, where status uses CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (:99) but cmd_sync walks $PWD (sync.sh:61, parse-entries.sh:23). The global stamp is confirmed: list-status.sh:146 uses one `segment-autosync-ts` for all repos, so with parallel sessions only the first repo to render in each 600s window gets synced. Overlaps status-2/status-3.
fix: Key the stamp by ledger path, e.g. `segment-autosync-ts-$(cksum <<<"$file" | cut -d' ' -f1)` or a builtin slug of $file. Spawn the child as `( cd "$(dirname "$(dirname "$file")")" && ... "$0" sync & )`, which removes the reliance on the caller's cd.

reason: bin/found-issues:321-323 returns the literal 'main' unverified. origin/HEAD is unset after `git remote add` + push (it is only set by clone or set-head). Combined with a non-GitHub remote, gh absent, or jq absent (the :287 gate), a master/trunk repo's commit annotations never close: both is-ancestor probes at sync.sh:190-191 fail silently. The PR half is narrower than claimed: it needs gh pr view to succeed while gh repo view fails. tests/cli-sync-default-branch.bats:49-58 pins only 'does not crash', not correctness.
fix: Before falling back, probe `git rev-parse --verify --quiet` for refs/remotes/origin/{main,master,trunk}, then local refs/heads/{main,master,trunk}, and `git config init.defaultBranch`. Return the first that exists. If none resolves, return empty (sync already skips commit closure when default_branch is empty) and print a one-line notice.

reason: sync.sh:189 treats any `git rev-parse --verify` failure as 'squash/force-push dropped it' and :198-200/:350 permanently rewrite the token to (commit-stale:). parse-entries.sh:230 only extracts `(commit: `, and no command reverses the demotion. A depth-1 clone (CI, cloud session checkouts) or an ambiguous 7-hex SHA in a large repo hits the same branch. The impact is fail-safe (the entry stays open rather than false-closing), but a valid closure path is destroyed and the destruction is committed. tests/cli-sync-commit-stale.bats:13 pins demotion only for a nonexistent SHA in a full clone.
fix: Before demoting, skip demotion (leave the annotation) when `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` prints true. Also skip it when `git cat-file -t "$sha" 2>&1` reports 'ambiguous'. Otherwise keep the current behavior.

reason: bin/found-issues:182 parses `--name-status` with core.quotepath at its default, so a non-ASCII src arrives as `"docs/caf\303\251.md"`, :199 never equals the raw path, and fi_detect_rename returns 1. fi_git_confirms_removed then sees the path absent from HEAD (:161) but present in history (:165, a pathspec works unquoted), so sync.sh:299-308 tombstones a live renamed entry irreversibly. That is a false close, but it requires a non-ASCII filename plus a rename, so graded medium rather than high.
fix: `git -c core.quotepath=off log --diff-filter=R -M --name-status ...` at bin/found-issues:182. That is enough for non-ASCII. -z is only needed for tab/newline/quote in names.

reason: sync.sh:332 `corrected_line="${corrected_line/$rename_source/$rename_target}"`: on bash >=5.2 (patsub_replacement on by default; Debian 12, Ubuntu 24.04, Homebrew) an `&` (or backslash) in a git-supplied rename target is expanded to the matched text. The unquoted pattern is a glob, but e_path is guarded (:222) and recovered_loc must itself equal a renamed path, so the glob half is near-theoretical. The suggested fix ('quote both operands') is not portable. On bash <=4.2 (macOS /bin/bash 3.2) the replacement inside a double-quoted ${//} does not undergo quote removal (compat42 semantics), so `"$rename_target"` would insert literal quotes. The same construct exists at annotate.sh:160; tests/cli-annotate-hook-auto.bats:249 uses a substring grep that would not catch stray quotes, so check it under /bin/bash 3.2.
fix: Use a prefix/suffix split with quoted patterns only (portable to 3.2): `pre="${corrected_line%%"$rename_source"*}"; post="${corrected_line#*"$rename_source"}"; corrected_line="$pre$rename_target$post"`. Do not quote the replacement operand.

reason: `IFS= read -r` keeps a trailing CR, :101 still matches, and :328 `printf '%s %s\n' "$fixed_line" "$closure_label"` puts the CR mid-line. The rename append at :334 behaves the same, as do resolve.sh:147 and annotate.sh:164/:534. Git for Windows defaults to core.autocrlf=true, so CRLF working-tree ledgers are the default there. Whether MSYS2 bash's read preserves CR (no igncr) is the runtime hinge. The impact is cosmetic plus diff noise.
fix: In each append site: `local cr=""; [[ $line == *$'\r' ]] && { cr=$'\r'; line=${line%$'\r'}; }` then `printf '%s %s%s\n' "$fixed_line" "$closure_label" "$cr"`.
repro: In Git Bash with autocrlf=true, check out a ledger (or unix2dos it), close an entry via tombstone or a merged PR, then run `grep -c $'\r (fixed' docs/found-issues.md` and expect 1.

reason: archive.sh:95 `IFS=$'\t' read -r date line`: tab is IFS whitespace, so trailing tabs are stripped from `line`, and :148 `-x` then no longer matches the active line. The entry is re-appended to the archive on every run (needs a hand-edited [fixed] line ending in a tab; sync/resolve always end lines with ')'). For (b), the count rule (:99) can select one of two byte-identical lines, while :148 deletes every identical copy. That loses one duplicate copy only, no unique content. Both are rare.
fix: Remove by line number: have the pass-1 awk emit `NR\tdate\tline`, select NRs in bash, then `awk 'NR==FNR{d[$1];next} !(FNR in d)' nrs_file "$file" >"$tmp"`. Read with `IFS= read -r rec` plus parameter-expansion splitting. This also fixes ledger-3 (awk has no binary mode).

reason: sync.sh:430 `archive_output="$(cmd_archive 2>&1 || true)"` and :432 print only on *moved*entries*. A cutoff failure (archive.sh:54-56; e.g. busybox/Alpine `date`, which rejects both `-v-30d` and `-d '30 days ago'`) or a missing ledger is fully hidden, and sync exits 0. Partial nuance: because of `|| true`, set -e is suspended inside cmd_archive, so an mv failure still reaches the 'moved' printf and does get surfaced along with the error text.
fix: `archive_output="$(cmd_archive 2>&1)" && arc=0 || arc=$?`. When arc is non-zero, print the output to stderr. Returning non-zero from sync is optional; a visible message is enough.

reason: The sync loop (sync.sh:100-101) and the archive awk (archive.sh:65) match `- [open]`/`- [fixed]` lines inside `<<<<<<<`...`>>>>>>>` regions. fi_entries skips those regions (parse-entries.sh:330-332), and fi_has_conflict_markers exists (:48) but neither sync nor archive calls it. SessionStart sync (session-start.sh:366) therefore mutates a conflicted ledger unattended, and an explicit archive can remove one side's line. The impact is confusion during resolution, not silent loss outside the conflict.
fix: At the top of cmd_sync (after file resolution) and cmd_archive, add `if fi_has_conflict_markers "$file"; then fi_err "<cmd>: ledger has merge-conflict markers — skipped"; return 0; fi`.

reason: annotate.sh:533 (and :154) runs `printf | grep -Fxq` for every ledger line, including headers and blanks, whenever auto_set is non-empty, so about 2 process creations per line. Exact-content membership means byte-identical duplicate lines are all annotated (:534 / :164). It also belongs to the pipefail family (hook-1/cli-9): bin/found-issues:29 sets pipefail, so a large auto_set could make grep -q's early exit SIGPIPE printf and fail the match. In practice auto_set is far below the pipe buffer, so that part is theoretical.
fix:
Gate on `[[ $line == "- ["* ]]` first, then use the builtin `[[ $'
'$auto_set == *$'
'"$line"$'
'* ]]` (auto_set already ends in a newline, :502). After a match, remove that one occurrence from auto_set (`auto_set="${auto_set/"$line"$'
'/}"`; pattern-side quoting is 3.2-safe) so a selection annotates at most one copy.
